text:
ana: quick question — we have a UX/telemetry gap for requests that get routed from org-key -> project-key fallback. who should be billed / surfaced in console: the originating org or the effective project? :thinking:

michael: my vote: bill the origin org (they started the request) but show effective project as the executor in telemetry. that matches expectations and keeps chargebacks sane.

srinivas: +1 on billing origin, but enforcement (rate limit, quota) needs to be applied to effective key otherwise noisy tenants could bypass project limits.
kari: important for console: customers expect the dashboard to say "requested by X" and "served by Y". can we show both with a simple toggle?

ana: @michael what about cross-org SA impersonation flows for dedicated pools? will origin billing still make sense there?
michael: good call — for dedicated pools we might want configurable attribution. default to origin org but allow tenant admins to opt-into "executor billing" for isolated pools. add a flag in console.

srinivas: telemetry-wise, we need a canonical attribution field so alerts and regressions are consistent. proposal: add three fields: origin_id, effective_id, attribution_mode (origin|effective). keep attribution_mode stable per request and emit to traces.
kari: console: show attribution_mode badge on per-route heatmaps, and a link to a short tooltip explaining policy. product ok with that?

ana: sounds fine. small UX ask: when mode=origin, still surface the effective_id in logs (collapsed by default). customers always ask who actually served the request.

infra-bot: note: adding two IDs to every trace increases trace size ~8%. recommend sampling or compressing for high-volume endpoints.
srinivas: agree on sampling. suggested approach: sample 100% for error traces and 1% for success traces, but keep aggregated counters 100% (attribution counters).
michael: implementable plan:
- traces: sample_errors=100% sample_success=1%
- metrics: increment origin.{org}.tokens and effective.{proj}.tokens per request
- logs: retain full ids for 7 days, then roll up

kari: UX rollout proposal: canary in console beta for 10 orgs (selected by usage pattern) -> 2-week telemetry eval -> full opt-in flag for customers -> 6-week default rollout.

nana: do we need a migration path for existing billing dashboards? existing dashboards assume single owner metric. ops will need to map old metric -> origin or effective.
michael: plan to emit both old_compatible.metric (maps to origin) and new split metrics. keep old_compatible for 90 days with a deprecation notice.
srinivas: telemetry team: we should update alerting runbooks to reference new metrics. expect some false positives during rollout.

deploy-bot: canary feature flag "attribution-dual-ids" enabled in prod for 10 orgs at 2026-05-02T15:00Z.
kari: followups: 1) docs for console labels 2) samples & storage impact analysis 3) UX mock for badge/tooltips. I'll own docs + UX mock.
michael: I'll own metrics emission and billing compatibility. srinivas — infra + tracing sampling?
srinivas: will do. I'll post an infra PR with sampling config & perf numbers. expect ~2 days for bench and PR.
nana: thumbs up. can we sync tomorrow 9am PT to review PR + mock?
michael: yes.
kari: calendar invite sent. :calendar:
